data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"A panel of non-experts following a checklist is less reliable than a single expert because checklists cannot capture the 'conditional logic' (context-dependent weighting) required for high-stakes verifiable outcomes, making any perceived gain a result of simple task-decomposition that ignores systemic edge cases.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The task is purely algorithmic or procedural with no hidden dependencies.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"The checklist is dynamically adaptive to the context of the specific case.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Expert intuition operates as a high-dimensional pattern recognition system that weights variables non-linearly; checklists force a linear, additive weighting that fails when the interaction between variables is the primary driver of the outcome.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
